title: Alert, write the runbook and replay a synthetic incident
problem: Signals only help if they reach a person as a decision. An on-call responder woken by "drift detected" needs to know whether inputs shifted, labels are late, the model degraded or a pipeline broke, because each has a different first action. Only a replay of a known incident shows whether the monitor says the right thing.
context: Final task of the pack. The learner scripts a synthetic incident with injected causes, for example a pipeline fault, then gradual input drift, then a label delay, and replays it through the monitor. This is where production readiness has something real to assess.
impact: A monitor that pages without telling the responder what to do is noise. This task is the difference.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Alerts distinguish input drift, prediction drift, performance degradation, missing labels and a malformed batch, and each alert names the evidence behind it (statistics, coverage, rejected rows).

Where signals overlap, the alert logic combines them to separate competing explanations; for example prediction drift with no input drift and a recent pipeline fault is not reported as model degradation.
A scripted synthetic incident with at least three injected causes is replayed end to end, and the alerts raised match the injected causes in order.
A runbook gives, for each alert kind, what it means, the evidence to look at first, and the first action.
A person with only the README can run the incident replay and see the alerts in under a minute.
Someone other than the learner reads one alert from the replay and the runbook, decides the first action, and justifies it. The result is recorded, including where they hesitated.
Automated tests run the replay and check the alert sequence, and pass at the submitted revision.
The learner explains how overlapping signals are combined into one alert, one rejected alternative (for example an alert per statistic), and which real incident the replay would handle badly.

constraints: Standard library plus a test runner only. No alerting service or scheduler.
No network access and no model API. Every input is synthetic and generated or checked in by the learner.
AC-outside-check requires a real person. A simulated or model-performed walkthrough does not satisfy it, and recording one as satisfied is fabricated evidence.
Do not push to a remote, publish a package or deploy anything as part of this task.

scope.description: Turning signals into decisions and proving it on a replayed incident.

investigation_areas: Which combination of signals points at each cause, and which combinations are ambiguous
What a responder needs in the first thirty seconds of reading an alert
Where a first-time reader actually hesitates, discovered by watching one
testing_expectations: Run the project's own test suite. State the exact command in the design; the learner chooses the runner and the layout.
Perform the quickstart on a clean clone before claiming AC-quickstart.
documentation_requirements: README quickstart, alert runbook and the operations note.
Record the outside walkthrough result verbatim, including where the person hesitated.
